questions.question: Which states have the most linked pairs whose two sources disagree on surname?
questions.text:
The states with the most linked pairs whose two sources disagree on surname are **NSW** (241 pairs), **VIC** (199 pairs), and **QLD** (134 pairs), all where both records are from the same state. Other notable states include **WA** (62 pairs) and **SA** (60 pairs).

Most disagreements occur within the same state, with NSW having the highest count.
questions.sql:
SELECT a.state AS left_state, b.state AS right_state, COUNT(*) AS disagree_links
FROM workspace.lakematch.lm_links k
JOIN workspace.lakematch.lm_left_valid a ON a.rec_id = k.l_id
JOIN workspace.lakematch.lm_right_valid b ON b.rec_id = k.r_id
WHERE a.surname IS NOT NULL AND b.surname IS NOT NULL
  AND a.state IS NOT NULL AND b.state IS NOT NULL
  AND lower(trim(a.surname)) <> lower(trim(b.surname))
GROUP BY a.state, b.state
ORDER BY disagree_links DESC
questions.description: You want to see which combinations of states from the left and right sources have the highest number of linked pairs where the surnames disagree between the two sources.

questions.question: How many merges in the last run produced entities of more than 5 records?
questions.text: In the last run, there were **0 merges** that produced entities with more than 5 records. This means no entity contained more than 5 records after merging.
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS merges_over_5_records
FROM (
  SELECT mdm_id
  FROM workspace.lakematch.lm_crosswalk
  WHERE mdm_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY mdm_id
  HAVING COUNT(record_key) > 5
)
questions.description: You want to know how many resolved entities (merges) have more than 5 records in total.

questions.question: What is the precision of the links by the number of empty fields in the left record?
questions.text:
The precision of the links by the number of empty fields in the left record is as follows:
- **0 empty fields**: precision is **0.994** (1,932 links)
- **1 empty field**: precision is **0.984** (434 links)
- **2 empty fields**: precision is **1.000** (32 links)
- **3 empty fields**: precision is **1.000** (1 link)

Precision remains very high across all groups, with perfect precision observed for records with 2 or 3 empty fields.
questions.sql:
WITH left_fields AS (
  SELECT rec_id,
    (CASE WHEN given_name IS NULL OR trim(given_name) = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
     CASE WHEN surname IS NULL OR trim(surname) = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
     CASE WHEN street_number IS NULL OR trim(street_number) = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
     CASE WHEN address_1 IS NULL OR trim(address_1) = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
     CASE WHEN address_2 IS NULL OR trim(address_2) = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
     CASE WHEN suburb IS NULL OR trim(suburb) = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
     CASE WHEN postcode IS NULL OR trim(postcode) = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
     CASE WHEN state IS NULL OR trim(state) = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
     CASE WHEN date_of_birth IS NULL OR trim(date_of_birth) = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END +
     CASE WHEN soc_sec_id IS NULL OR trim(soc_sec_id) = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
    ) AS empty_fields
  FROM workspace.lakematch.lm_left_valid
)
, links_with_empty AS (
  SELECT l.l_id, l.r_id, lf.empty_fields
  FROM workspace.lakematch.lm_links l
  JOIN left_fields lf ON l.l_id = lf.rec_id
)
, true_links AS (
  SELECT l.l_id, l.r_id, lf.empty_fields
  FROM workspace.lakematch.lm_links l
  JOIN left_fields lf ON l.l_id = lf.rec_id
  JOIN workspace.lakematch.lm_eval_truth t ON l.l_id = t.l_id AND l.r_id = t.r_id
)
SELECT le.empty_fields,
  ROUND(try_divide(COUNT(tl.l_id) * 1.0,COUNT(le.l_id)), 3) AS precision,
  COUNT(le.l_id) AS total_links
FROM links_with_empty le
LEFT JOIN true_links tl ON le.l_id = tl.l_id AND le.r_id = tl.r_id
GROUP BY le.empty_fields
ORDER BY le.empty_fields ASC
questions.description: You want to see the precision of the links grouped by how many empty fields the left record has.

questions.question: How many links did the model make and what is their average match probability?
questions.text: The model made **2,399 links** with an **average match probability of 0.982**. This average is calculated from all links where the match probability was present.
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_links, AVG(p) AS avg_match_probability FROM workspace.lakematch.lm_links WHERE p IS NOT NULL
questions.description: You want to know the total number of links the model has made and the average match probability of those links.

questions.question: How many rows were quarantined in each source?
questions.text: There were **4 rows quarantined** in the left source and **2 rows quarantined** in the right source. The left source had twice as many quarantined rows as the right source.
questions.sql:
SELECT 'left' AS source, COUNT(*) AS quarantined_rows FROM workspace.lakematch.lm_left_quarantine
UNION ALL
SELECT 'right' AS source, COUNT(*) AS quarantined_rows FROM workspace.lakematch.lm_right_quarantine
questions.description: You want to know the number of rows that were quarantined in each data source, left and right.

questions.question: What share of the true pairs in the evaluation sample did the model link?
questions.text: The model linked **95.2%** of the true pairs in the evaluation sample. This means that out of all true pairs, 95.2% were successfully identified by the model.
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(try_divide(COUNT(linked.l_id) * 1.0,COUNT(truth.l_id)), 3) AS recall
FROM workspace.lakematch.lm_eval_truth truth
LEFT JOIN workspace.lakematch.lm_links linked
  ON truth.l_id = linked.l_id AND truth.r_id = linked.r_id
questions.description: You want to know the proportion of true pairs from the evaluation sample that the model successfully linked, which is the recall metric.

questions.question: How many labels has each reviewer given in the arbitration app, by decision?
questions.text: There is one reviewer (ID starting with fbb39591) who has given **3 'retract'** decisions and **3 'unsure'** decisions in the arbitration app. This data covers only these two decision types for this reviewer.
questions.sql:
SELECT `reviewer`, `decision`, COUNT(*) AS label_count
FROM `workspace`.`lakematch`.`lm_review_labels`
WHERE `reviewer` IS NOT NULL AND `decision` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY `reviewer`, `decision`
ORDER BY `reviewer`, `decision`
questions.description: You want to see how many labels each reviewer has given in the arbitration app, broken down by the type of decision they made.

questions.question: How many pairs in the review queue have no label yet, by queue reason?
questions.text: There are **1,997 pairs** in the review queue with **no label yet** and the queue reason is **"other"**. This is the only queue reason represented in the data.
questions.sql:
SELECT q.queue_reason, COUNT(*) AS pairs_no_label
FROM workspace.lakematch.lm_review_queue q
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT l_id, r_id, MAX(labelled_at) AS latest_labelled_at
  FROM workspace.lakematch.lm_review_labels
  GROUP BY l_id, r_id
) r ON q.l_id = r.l_id AND q.r_id = r.r_id
WHERE r.latest_labelled_at IS NULL
GROUP BY q.queue_reason
questions.description: You want to see the number of pairs in the review queue that do not have any label yet, grouped by the reason they are in the queue.

questions.question: Show precision, recall and F1 for every model version in the run history.
questions.text: For model version **workspace.lakematch.lakematch_febrl4 v3**, the precision is **0.9925**, recall is **0.9524**, and F1 score is **0.972**. This is the only model version in the run history with all three metrics available.
questions.sql: SELECT model_version, precision, recall, f1 FROM workspace.lakematch.lm_review_runs WHERE precision IS NOT NULL AND recall IS NOT NULL AND f1 IS NOT NULL ORDER BY created_at
questions.description: You want to see the precision, recall, and F1 score for each model version in the history of evaluation runs.

questions.question: How are the candidate pairs distributed across match-probability bands of 0.1?
questions.text: Candidate pairs are distributed across match-probability bands as follows: the **0.0 band** contains **22,553 pairs**, while the **0.9 band** contains **2,447 pairs**. Only these two bands are represented in the sample data. The majority of candidate pairs fall into the lowest probability band, with a much smaller number in the highest band.
questions.sql:
SELECT try_divide(FLOOR(`p`*10),10) AS p_band, COUNT(*) AS candidate_count
FROM `workspace`.`lakematch`.`lm_scores`
WHERE `p` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY try_divide(FLOOR(`p`*10),10)
ORDER BY p_band ASC
questions.description: You want to see how candidate pairs are distributed across different match probability ranges, grouped in bands of 0.1 from 0 to 1.
